text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Province of Limburg to investigate Benzine leak at DSM chemical complex (p1)
- DAF gives boost to Paccar trucks first quarter result (p3)
- US wins "Banana War" with Europe over preferential treatment for former colonies' exports. (p7)
VOLKSKRANT
- Dutch want EU states to hold off on sending ambassadors back to Iran. (p1)
- Queen's Day revels in Amsterdam fuelled by illegal beer sales. (p1)
- French insurer GAN hints at interest in tie-up with ING. (p2)
- Visiting Taiwan vice-premier will not speak to any Dutch government officials. (p4)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Queen's Day festivals around the country celebrated without trouble (p1)
- Dutch version of EU identity card will be most expensive in Europe (p1)
- Amsterdam police to increase cooperation with Antillean counterparts to tackle drug smuggling (p3)
- Brewer Heineken plans on-the-job testing for all 2000 production workers in the Netherlands. (p37)
- Consulting engineers Grontmij will look seriously at any takeover bid for the business.
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Possible extra European Summit meet on May 23 may be held in Noordwijk (p9)
- Dutch football team crushes San Marino (p17)
TROUW
- Father varrested for murder of two-year-old son.(p3)
- Shell resumes Nigerian oil production after resolution of tribal conflict. (p7)
